meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как можно было сказать, что я болею?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты уже закончил работу, Лёва?
examples.trans: Have you finished work already, Lyova?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'themselves', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я просто медицинскую книжку себе продлевал.
examples.trans: I was simply renewing my medical book.

examples.text: Ладно, давай закажем себе по коктейлю.

examples.trans: Take it for yourself, I do not want it yet.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Лёва, какую ерунду ты сейчас говоришь?

examples.text: Ей сейчас очень плохо после этой истории.
examples.trans: She feels awful right now after that whole story.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'feel', paired with 'почувствовать'.

examples.text: Я чувствую себя хорошо.
examples.trans: I feel well.

examples.text: Ты чувствуешь запах?
examples.trans: Can you smell that?

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, я за ними ухаживаю.
examples.trans: Thank you, I take good care of them.

examples.text: Спасибо за приглашение, я обязательно приду.
examples.trans: Thank you for the invitation, I will definitely come.

examples.text: Спасибо тебе большое за хорошие новости!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for the good news!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Подожди, ты сегодня был в больнице?
examples.trans: Wait, were you at the hospital today?

examples.text: Может, пойдёшь сегодня вечером с нами?
examples.trans: Maybe you will come out with us tonight?

examples.text: А кто ещё из девочек сегодня будет?
examples.trans: And who else of the girls will be here today?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Especially since I am a brilliant head chef.

examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

examples.text: Я знаю, что вам нельзя работать.
examples.trans: I know that you must not work.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё хорошо, мы уже скоро поедем.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, we will be going soon.

meanings.en: much, far, a lot (before a comparative)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ну хорошо, давай попробуем это сделать.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лежаться'). examples.trans: What are you talking about, anyone but Denis!

examples.text: Настя, стой, этот коктейль не тебе!
examples.trans: Nastya, stop, that cocktail is not for you!

examples.text: Этот коктейль до конца допивать нельзя!
examples.trans: You must not drink that cocktail all the way to the bottom!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Дело в том, что я тоже Катю позвала.
examples.trans: The thing is that I invited Katya too.

examples.text: Знаешь, если честно, мне они тоже надоели.
examples.trans: You know, to be honest, I was tired of it too.

examples.text: Я тоже.
examples.trans: Me too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Значит, она точно к нам придёт!
examples.trans: That means she will definitely come to our place!

examples.text: Вот откуда, значит, это новоселье вдруг взялось!
examples.trans: So that is where this housewarming suddenly came from!

examples.text: Значит, тебе на самом деле нравятся богатые!
examples.trans: That means you actually like rich guys!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Кате точно нужно надёжное мужское плечо.
examples.trans: Katya definitely needs a reliable man's shoulder.

examples.text: Скажи, у тебя точно всё в порядке?
examples.trans: Tell me, is everything really alright with you?

examples.text: Значит, она точно к нам придёт!
examples.trans: That means she will definitely come to our place!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Поставь телефон на громкую связь.
examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

examples.text: Вы лучше спокойно дома отдохните.
examples.trans: You had better rest quietly at home.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.text: Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Я приду завтра.
examples.trans: I'll come tomorrow.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.
